description: User Language programs (ULPs) shipped with EAGLE 9.6.0 in <EAGLE>\examples\ulps\examples, part A: bills of material, CAM helpers, assembly and pick-and-place data, drill, DXF/image and fabrication/test formats, signal-integrity and 3D/IDF exports, board statistics and length measurement, and importers for DXF, Gerber, bitmaps, netlists and other CAD formats. Run them from an editor command line with RUN <file>.ulp [args]; this needs the interactive editor, which after the June 2026 licensing shutdown stops at the Autodesk sign-in window.

tools.name: bom.ulp
tools.description: Exports a project's bill of materials from the schematic, including part attributes. The dialog lists either every part or parts grouped by value, lets you pick an assembly variant and switch attribute columns on or off, and saves the list as text, CSV or HTML.
tools.usage: RUN bom.ulp   (Schematic Editor; dialog: Parts | Values, List attributes, Text | CSV | HTML, Save...)
tools.notes: Dialog-driven, no command-line options. For a scripted BOM, read the <parts> of the .sch XML directly.

tools.name: cam2dxf.ulp
tools.description: Converts the sections of a CAM job into a script that exports DXF data layer by layer from the board or schematic. Without a file name it asks for the CAM job.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: CAM job file (.cam) whose sections define the layer sets.

tools.notes: Tip from the ULP: ASSIGN Shift+Ctrl+Alt+P 'run cam2dxf;'. Since 8.6 the CAM Processor can also write DXF directly and dxf.ulp exports a whole drawing.

tools.name: cam2image.ulp
tools.description: Turns a CAM job into a script that exports each section as an image (EXPORT IMAGE), monochrome or color, at a chosen resolution and image type. It works from the board or schematic editor and executes the generated commands when it ends.
tools.usage: RUN cam2image [ filename monochrome|color resolution imagetype ]
tools.example:
RUN cam2image myjob.cam monochrome 150 .bmp
RUN cam2image myjob.cam color 300 .tif
tools.notes: See exp2image.ulp for a layer list instead of a CAM job.

tools.name: cam2print.ulp
tools.description: Converts a CAM job into PRINT commands, one print per section; with PDF as output file the prints go into a PDF. Use it to print a set of layer combinations defined once in a CAM job.
tools.notes: lbr-assign.scr contains commented examples that bind cam2printer/cam2dxf to keys.

tools.name: centroid-screamingcircuits-smd.ulp
tools.description: Writes a centroid (pick-and-place) file in the format expected by the Screaming Circuits assembly service: surface-mount parts only, comma-delimited in inches with the columns RefDes, Layer, LocationX, LocationY and Rotation, saved as <board>_centroid.csv. Run it in the Board Editor; it refuses to work anywhere else.
tools.notes: Stops with an error when started outside the layout editor. Since 9.5 the CAM Processor also has a built-in Pick&Place output.

tools.name: mount-smd-tht.ulp
tools.description: Generates placement data for mounting machines with SMD and through-hole parts optionally in separate files (<board>-smd.mnt, <board>-tht.mnt or one <board>.mnt). Use it when SMD and through-hole parts are placed in separate assembly steps.
tools.notes: Other mounting-data variants: mount.ulp, mountsmd.ulp, mount-marks.ulp.

tools.name: mount.ulp and mountsmd.ulp
tools.description: Mounting-machine data from the board. mount.ulp writes <board>.mnt (value;x;y;rotation;name in mil) for all parts populated in the current assembly variant; mountsmd.ulp writes top and bottom SMD files (<board>.mnt, <board>.mnb; name x y rotation value package in mm). Coordinates are the centre of the pads' extent, which may differ from the part origin.
tools.notes: Choose the assembly variant before running; unpopulated parts are skipped.

tools.name: mount-marks.ulp and mount-marks-smd.ulp
tools.description: Mounting-machine data for top and bottom with element origin coordinates in mm, one line 'Name x y Rotation Value Package' per SMD element, plus the positions of all elements taken from a library named 'marks' (variable def_lbr in the source), e.g. fiducial marks. mount-marks-smd.ulp is the revised variant (1.0.2) that avoids duplicate lines and displays the exported data.
tools.usage: RUN mount-marks.ulp | RUN mount-marks-smd.ulp   (Board Editor; dialog)
tools.notes: Unlike mount.ulp these use the element origin, not the pad centre. Change def_lbr if your mark footprints live in another library.

tools.name: mount-trace.ulp
tools.description: Assists manual assembly: builds a list of top-side parts grouped by equal value and steps through it, highlighting all parts of the current value. Options move the pointer forward or back, show a count/value/package dialog, or mirror the board to work on the bottom side.

parameters.name: -L
parameters.description: Generate the trace list from the current board.
Show next / previous value; ++ and -- also open a dialog with counts, value and package.
Reset the pointer.

parameters.name: -M
parameters.description: Mirror the board (bottom to top), save it under an extended name and build the list from that side.

tools.notes: The ULP suggests assigning + and - to function keys with ASSIGN.

tools.name: smd-coordinate.ulp
tools.description: Writes the coordinates of all SMD pads of the layout into two files, <board>.smt for the top layer and <board>.smb for the bottom layer, for example for stencil or dispenser equipment. The output lists pad positions rather than part positions.
tools.notes: Pad-level data; for part placement use mount*.ulp.

tools.name: dxf.ulp
tools.description: Converts the current board or schematic into a DXF file. Options add a file-name suffix, choose mm or inch, force the vector font, draw wires with their real width and fill areas.

parameters.name: -s suffix
parameters.description: Appended to the output file name.

parameters.name: -u mm|inch
parameters.description: Unit for coordinates and dimensions.

parameters.name: -a / -w / -f
parameters.description: Always vector font / use wire width / fill areas.

tools.example: RUN dxf -s _s1 -u mm -w   # -> <name>_s1.dxf in mm with real wire widths
tools.notes: Works in board and schematic (current sheet).

tools.name: exp2image.ulp
tools.description: Exports the current schematic, board or library object as an image with selectable layers, monochrome or color, resolution and image type. Defaults are color, 150 dpi and BMP with all layers of the drawing type.
tools.example:
RUN exp2image monochrome 150 .tif 1 17 18 20
RUN exp2image color 150 .bmp 91 92 94 95 96
tools.notes: Wraps EXPORT IMAGE with a DISPLAY of the chosen layers.

tools.name: drillcfg.ulp
tools.description: Generates a drill configuration (drill rack) file <board>.drl for the current board in mm or inch; the file can be edited before saving, and the ULP is also handy for reviewing the drills used on a board. The built-in help names it as the tool for creating drill rack files.
tools.notes: A drill rack file is only needed when a drill station driver cannot generate the drill definitions itself (help topic 'Drill Rack File'); format: one line per tool, e.g. T01 0.010.

tools.name: drillegend-stack.ulp
tools.description: Adds a drill legend (table of drill symbols, diameters and counts) to the board in layer 144 by default and can place drill symbols on the board; it can also write the drill configuration for the CAM Processor, with tools and diameters sorted in the same order as the legend. Use it to document drill sizes on a fabrication drawing layer.
tools.notes: Drills are rounded in this ULP, so do not combine it with Options > Set > Drill set. The symbol list can be extended in the source.

tools.name: drill-aid.ulp
tools.description: Helps manual drilling by drawing small circles in layer 116 inside the drill holes of pads, vias and holes, leaving a small centring mark in the copper when layer 116 is output with the bottom layers. It is meant for hand-drilled prototype boards.
tools.notes: Remove the marks with DISPLAY 116 only, GROUP, DELETE, then LAYER -116.

tools.name: dif40.ulp
tools.description: Exports the board in DIF 4.0, a production and test format defined by Digitaltest GmbH, to <board>.dif. User-definable parameters are at the top of the program.
tools.notes: Check the 'user definable parameters' section of the source before use.

tools.name: fabmaster.ulp
tools.description: Writes the board in Fabmaster FATF REV 11.1 format (<board>.fab) for fabrication and test tools. Run it from the Board Editor; the program text documents the format details.
tools.notes: Details are documented in the program text.

tools.name: unidat.ulp
tools.description: Exports the design in UNIDAT format (<board>.uni plus a reference file <board>.ref) with component, part number, tolerance and property data. Use it to hand assembly and test data to tools that read UNIDAT.
tools.notes: The program reads board data and, where available, schematic data.

tools.name: ipc-d-356.ulp
tools.description: Generates a netlist in IPC-D-356 format (<board>.ipc) from the board, used by fabricators for electrical (bare-board) testing. The netlist lets the manufacturer compare the finished bare board against the design.
tools.notes: IPC-D-356 allows at most 14 characters per net name; shorten longer names first.

tools.name: export-ict-netlist-pad-coordinates.ulp
tools.description: Exports an in-circuit-test netlist with pad and SMD coordinates, one line per contact in the form Net Part.Pad Layer X Y, to <board>.ict. Test-fixture builders can use it to locate a contact for every net.
tools.notes: Unconnected pads are listed under NOSIGNAL.

tools.name: hyperlynx.ulp
tools.description: Exports the board to the HyperLynx signal-integrity transfer format (.HYP, plus a .REF file). Supports 1 to 16 layer boards, wire arcs, oblong pads and via stacks.
tools.notes: Layer mapping for multilayer boards is listed in the #usage text (e.g. 4 layers = 1, 2, 15, 16).

tools.name: siwave.ulp
tools.description: Exports the board to the Ansys Neutral File format (.ANF) for Ansys SIwave, based on hyperlynx.ulp; 1 to 16 layer boards are supported. It lets the board be analysed in Ansys SIwave.
tools.notes: Same layer conventions as hyperlynx.ulp.

tools.name: eagleidfexporter.ulp
tools.description: Generates IDF board (.emn) and library (.emp) files from the board for import into mechanical CAD tools, using package outlines and HEIGHT attributes for component heights. IDF passes the board outline and component bodies to MCAD tools without the cloud-based STEP export.
tools.notes: Set a HEIGHT attribute on parts for realistic bodies. An offline alternative to EXPORTSTEP.

tools.name: generate-3d-idf-data.ulp and gen-3d-idf-pac.ulp
tools.description: generate-3d-idf-data.ulp exports 3D data from the board in IDF format, taking the board outline from layer 50 and part heights from layers 57 (top) and 58 (bottom), which it can create if missing. gen-3d-idf-pac.ulp prepares that height data inside the current package in the Library Editor.
tools.usage: RUN generate-3d-idf-data.ulp (Board Editor) | RUN gen-3D-pac-idf [ high-top high-bottom ] (Package Editor, heights in mm)
tools.notes: The #usage refers to doc/generate_3d_data_eng.pdf for details.

tools.name: ecadio.ulp
tools.description: Uploads the board to the ecad.io web service to create a 3D PCB for MCAD use. It sends the board data to an external website rather than writing a local file.
tools.notes: Needs internet access and an external web service; its availability after EAGLE's retirement is not guaranteed.

tools.name: mill-outlines.ulp
tools.description: Exports milling (isolation routing) and drilling data for a board layout as an EAGLE script, HPGL, ISEL or CNC output, with many options for tool diameters, contour and pour isolation, mirroring for bottom-side milling, milling of the board dimension and drill output. It targets PCB prototyping mills that isolate tracks by milling around them.
tools.example: RUN mill-outlines.ulp   # choose HPGL, tool diameters, top/bottom, then OK
tools.notes: Also writes auxiliary files such as <board>.pen and <board>-cmd.txt; the dialog's help images ship alongside the ULP.

tools.name: outlines.ulp
tools.description: Generates outline (isolation contour) data of the copper in one layer as an EAGLE script or HPGL, with a given contour width, for prototyping mills. Run it in the Board Editor once for each copper layer to be milled.
tools.usage: RUN outlines [ device [ width [ layer [ filename ]]]]

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Script or HPGL.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Outline width in mm.

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: 1..16 (0 = active layer).

tools.notes: mill-outlines.ulp is the more complete milling exporter.

tools.name: gluemark.ulp and glueout.ulp
tools.description: SMD glue-dispenser data in two steps: gluemark.ulp places glue-point circles on layers 111 (top) and 112 (bottom) from circles defined in the packages' tGlue layer (or one default point at the centre of the tPlace outline); after editing those layers, glueout.ulp writes the top and bottom glue data from them. Both run in the Board Editor.
tools.usage: RUN gluemark.ulp; then RUN glueout.ulp   (Board Editor)
tools.example:
RUN gluemark.ulp
RUN glueout.ulp   # -> gluetop.dat, gluebot.dat
tools.notes: Adapt the function outputdata in glueout.ulp to the dispenser's format.

tools.name: dose-pro.ulp
tools.description: Generates control data for the solder-paste dispenser unit of 'Martin' on Bungard drilling/milling machines: SMD pad coordinates for top (<board>.plt) and bottom (<board>.plb) and tool information (<board>.dod). Run it in the Board Editor after the SMD layout is final.
tools.notes: Machine-specific format.

tools.name: part2html.ulp
tools.description: Writes the board's part list as an HTML file (<board>.htm), for example to publish on an intranet. It runs in the Board Editor and asks where to save the file.
tools.notes: bom.ulp offers HTML output from the schematic with attributes and variants.

tools.name: count.ulp
tools.description: Counts pads, vias, SMDs and holes of the board, shows the result in a dialog and can save it as <board>.txt, useful for quoting and drilling estimates. Run it in the Board Editor, for example when estimating drilling effort.
tools.notes: statistic-brd.ulp gives a far more detailed breakdown.

tools.name: statistic-brd.ulp, statistic-sch.ulp and statistic-lbr.ulp
tools.description: Statistics tables: statistic-brd.ulp lists the elements of a layout (wires, vias, drills, pads, SMDs, polygons ...) with optional minimum-value checks, statistic-sch.ulp tabulates the parts of a schematic and writes a .rep report, and statistic-lbr.ulp reports library contents, shows which symbols and packages are used by device sets and can delete unused symbols. Use them to review a design or library before release.
tools.usage: RUN statistic-brd.ulp (Board) | RUN statistic-sch.ulp (Schematic) | RUN statistic-lbr.ulp (Library)
tools.notes: Change the table units with the variable uval in the ULP source.

tools.name: statistic-copper-plane.ulp
tools.description: Estimates the copper area of layers by rendering and evaluating bitmaps of each layer, together with the board area. Use it when a copper-area figure is needed, for example for plating or copper-balance considerations.
tools.notes: No objects may lie outside the board contour in layer 20 Dimension, otherwise the result is wrong.

tools.name: length.ulp
tools.description: Calculates the routed length of signals (wires in layers 1-16) and lists airwires separately. With several signal names it also reports length differences in percent relative to the shortest, which helps with length matching.
tools.usage: run length [name | name* | *name | *name*] | run length name [name name ...]
tools.example:
run length d0 d2 d7 A*
run length *
tools.notes: Parallel tracks and polygons are not taken into account.

tools.name: lpp.ulp
tools.description: Measures the trace length between two given pads (element/pad pairs), following wires, micro, blind and buried vias; with /G it does this for every signal of a previously defined GROUP. Other pads on the way are ignored.
tools.usage: RUN lpp Elementname Padname Elementname Padname [...] | RUN lpp /G
tools.notes: Branches with vias at the same location may give the wrong branch; such results are marked.

tools.name: length-freq-ri.ulp
tools.description: Lists all signals of a board with maximum frequency, length, area, resistance, minimum and maximum width and maximum current, as a quick first evaluation of the layout; saved as <board>.txt. It runs in the Board Editor and shows the list in a dialog before saving.
tools.notes: Simplified calculation; parallel tracks and polygons are ignored.

tools.name: export-class.ulp
tools.description: Exports the net classes of a board or schematic (widths, clearances, drills) as a script <project>-class.scr, so they can be applied to another design with SCRIPT. Run it in the board or schematic whose classes you want to reuse.
tools.example:
RUN export-class.ulp
# in the other design: SCRIPT myproject-class.scr
tools.notes: Units MIC, MM, MIL or INCH are selectable.

tools.name: export-error.ulp
tools.description: Exports or saves the DRC or ERC error list of the current board or schematic to a file. Use it to archive check results or share them with others.
tools.notes: The #usage text is German only and names the program export-errors; use the actual file name export-error.ulp with RUN.

tools.name: save-brd-variants.ulp
tools.description: Switches through all assembly variants and saves one board file per variant, named <file>-<variant>.brd (default for the default variant), as preparation for variant-specific CAM output. Invalid file-name characters are replaced with '_'.
tools.usage: RUN save-brd-variants.ulp   (schematic and board loaded and consistent)
tools.notes: eaglecon's -A option can also select a variant directly.

tools.name: import-dxf.ulp
tools.description: Imports DXF files containing polylines into a board, schematic or library as an editable script: choose origin, input units, scale factor and line width, then check the generated script and target layer before running it. Typical uses are board outlines and mechanical drawings from MCAD tools.
tools.usage: run import-dxf.ulp filename TargetLayer Units [Xorg Yorg lwidth scale scaleflags]

parameters.name: TargetLayer
parameters.description: Layer number 1-255 for the imported objects.

parameters.name: Units
parameters.description: 0 = imperial, 1 = metric.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Origin X/Y, line width, scale factor and a three-digit 0/1 flag saying whether Xorg, Yorg and width are scaled.

tools.notes: Typical use: board outline into layer 20 Dimension.

tools.name: import-gerber.ulp
tools.description: Imports Gerber files into a board by generating and loading a script, with dialogs for layer mapping, units, zero omission and absolute/incremental notation. Useful to recover or compare artwork.
tools.example: RUN import-gerber.ulp   # select myboard.GTL, map it to layer 1
tools.notes: The result is graphics (wires/polygons), not connected signals.

tools.name: import-bmp.ulp
tools.description: Imports a bitmap (up to 256 colors, of which at most 32 can be selected) by writing a script that draws rectangles for runs of equal-colored pixels, scaled by DPI, pixel size or aspect ratio. Typical use is logos on silkscreen or copper.
tools.usage: RUN import-bmp.ulp   (board, schematic or library; dialog)
tools.example: RUN import-bmp.ulp   # logo.bmp -> layer 21 tPlace at 600 dpi
tools.notes: Very small rectangles below the output device resolution will not reproduce; many rectangles slow the display.

tools.name: import-accel.ulp
tools.description: Imports boards, schematics or libraries that were exported from P-CAD, Altium or Protel to the ACCEL ASCII format. It is the route for bringing older P-CAD, Protel or Altium designs into EAGLE.
tools.notes: A large ULP (about 9800 lines); review the result with ERC/DRC.

tools.name: import-pads-powerpcb-v5.ulp
tools.description: Imports library data from a PADS PowerPCB V5.0 ASCII design database file into EAGLE, creating packages (footprints) and symbols; an option writes a separate library per package when the PADS file reuses package names with different parameters. Start it with a library open in the Library Editor.
tools.notes: eagle.scr adds it to the LBR/DEV/PAC menus as 'PADS package import'.

tools.name: import-ultiboard-ddf.ulp
tools.description: Imports Ultiboard PCB Design Data Files (DDF, versions 4.80 and 5.50) into an EAGLE board. Start it in the Board Editor and select the DDF file in the dialog.
tools.notes: Based on appendix A (file formats) of the Ultiboard user manual.

tools.name: cmd-net-list2sch.ulp and cmd-netscript2sch.ulp
tools.description: Draw net connections into a schematic whose parts are already placed: cmd-net-list2sch.ulp reads an EAGLE net list (or a single net given as net part pin part pin ...), cmd-netscript2sch.ulp reads an EAGLE netscript as exported by some PCB systems. Nets start with a 50 mil diagonal offset so they do not run over pins, and labels are added when a net continues on another sheet.
tools.usage: RUN cmd-net-list2sch [ netlist-file ] | RUN cmd-net-list2sch net part pin part pin ... | RUN cmd-netscript2sch
tools.example:
RUN cmd-net-list2sch hexapod.lst
RUN cmd-net-list2sch clk ic1 9 ic3 15
tools.notes: Check the result with ERC; a net crossing an unconnected pin could otherwise connect to it later.

tools.name: netlist-converter.ulp
tools.description: Converts a netlist from another CAD system (Multiwire, OrCAD, Tango or Mentor format) into an EAGLE netscript (.scr) and executes it with SCRIPT, for example to wire a board or schematic whose parts are already placed. A dialog selects the source format and file.
tools.example: RUN netlist-converter.ulp   # choose an OrCAD netlist
tools.notes: Part names in the netlist must match the element names in EAGLE.

tools.name: Felicitas_PCBSim.ulp
tools.description: Interface to the Felicitas PCBSim pre-layout simulation (PreSim): exports design data or the attributes of a selected instance, offers a setup page and re-imports simulation values, waiting for a file-based handshake. It is only useful with the external Felicitas PCBSim software installed.

parameters.name: /E
parameters.description: Export data.

parameters.name: /I
parameters.description: Export attributes of the selected instance.

parameters.name: /S
parameters.description: Setup options.

parameters.name: /RELOAD
parameters.description: Import simulation values.

tools.notes: Requires the external PCBSim software.

tools.name: designlink-order.ulp and designlink-lbr.ulp
tools.description: DesignLink ULPs for the distributor Farnell/Newark: designlink-order.ulp searches products for all schematic parts or in general, checks price and availability, stores found order codes as attributes and exports the order list; designlink-lbr.ulp embeds Farnell and/or Newark order codes into library devices. designlink-inc.ulp is their shared include file.

parameters.name: -general
parameters.description: General product search instead of searching all parts of the schematic.

parameters.name: -sop
parameters.description: Also use the package name in the search for more accurate results.

parameters.name: -both_oc
parameters.description: designlink-lbr: search Farnell and Newark and embed both order codes.

tools.notes: eagle.scr puts them in the 'Search and order' menu. They depend on the distributor's online service.

tools.name: pcb-service.ulp
tools.description: Requests a quote for a PCB layout service from PCBLayout.com (Royal Circuit Solutions) based on design data such as the pin count, and can upload files to that service. It opens a dialog and needs internet access.
tools.notes: eagle.scr adds it to the board editor menu as 'PCB Service'. It sends design data to an external web service, so use it only deliberately; availability after EAGLE's retirement is not guaranteed.
